gaps.note: Edit when Lori asks about Kickstarter.
Edit during Michael's answer about the biking hurdle.
Edit after Michael nods to Mark's challenge.

stage_a.note: Michael smiles and speaks clearly about the product, showing moderate engagement alongside neutral technical descriptions.
Michael shows engaged animation when talking about stepping into the future, alternating with subdued delivery.
The founders are polite and friendly, offering the bike to the panel, but maintain professional distance.

venture.description: A self-contained electric wheel that replaces the front wheel of almost any bicycle to convert it into an electric bike.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders introduce themselves, state their ask, and demonstrate how their electric wheel replaces a regular bicycle's front wheel.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks if he can try riding the bike to experience how the electric wheel performs.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michael agrees and offers to grab another bike so the other sharks can also try riding.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin asks what he needs to know before he begins riding the electric bike around the set.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Dakota explains that the bike rides exactly like a normal bicycle, with the only difference being the throttle.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara asks if anyone else on the panel wants to try riding the electric bike.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michael mentions that they have helmets available for the sharks to wear while riding the bikes.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Chris jokes that he would never wear a helmet on television because it would result in a blackmail photo.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin rides the bike and remarks that the experience of using the electric wheel is very cool.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara enthusiastically agrees with Kevin as she watches him ride the electric bike around the set.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara gets on a second electric bike and playfully announces she is going to catch Kevin.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michael encourages Barbara as she starts riding, noting that using the electric wheel is just like riding a bike.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Chris jokes about the blind chasing the blind as he watches Kevin and Barbara ride the electric bikes.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara asks where the brake is located and is instructed that she has to pedal backwards to stop.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori watches the other sharks ride the electric bikes and expresses her amazement at the product.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin continues riding the electric bike around the set, enjoying the demonstration of the product.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark cheers and expresses his enjoyment as he watches Kevin and Barbara ride the electric bikes.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara remarks that riding the electric bike is highly enjoyable and feels like a magical experience.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks if the founders launched their electric wheel product on crowdfunding platforms like Kickstarter and Indiegogo.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michael confirms they launched four months ago and successfully raised over one point two million dollars on Kickstarter.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara expresses her impressed reaction upon hearing the significant amount of funding raised on Kickstarter.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michael adds that they have sold an additional two hundred thousand dollars directly through their own website.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark asks if the founders are currently shipping products to customers or if they are still in the prototype phase.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Dakota answers that they will begin shipping their first production units to customers in about two months.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara points out that the panel has not yet heard the retail price of the electric wheel.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori agrees with Barbara and asks the founders to state the retail price of the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michael states that the electric wheel conversion kit will retail for nine hundred and fifty dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara asks if it would be cheaper for a consumer to simply purchase a fully electric bike instead.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Dakota replies that the cost comparison ultimately depends on the specific electric bike model being considered.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara asserts that a consumer can easily purchase a complete electric bike for under nine hundred and fifty dollars.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michael acknowledges cheaper bikes exist but argues their quality is lower, noting pre-order customers have not raised this concern.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Chris asks if their market opportunity is strictly limited to retrofitting existing traditional bicycles that lack electric capabilities.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michael explains that regular biking presents a hurdle for people who get anxious about sweating on their commute.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Chris states that electric bikes are the future and all shipped bikes will eventually feature an electric option.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Chris asks the founders directly if they ever plan to manufacture their own complete electric bicycles.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michael interrupts the current line of questioning to show the panel another product they have brought.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Dakota clarifies that they do not currently make standard bikes, but have created something completely different.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara remarks that the new, smaller electric bike the founders are showing is very cool.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Chris mentions he loves the banana seat on the new product and asks what it is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michael demonstrates how to sit on the new small bike, noting that it looks really fun to ride.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara expresses her strong liking for the new small electric bike being demonstrated.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michael explains the small bike's tight turning radius, extreme nimbleness, and ability to easily fit into a car trunk.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara asks to clarify if they are also selling the small bikes for nine hundred and fifty dollars.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori asks the founders how much the newly demonstrated small electric bike costs to purchase.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michael states that the small bike costs two hundred dollars in addition to the price of the electric wheel.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Chris asks whether the founders are prioritizing their time on developing the new small bike or the electric wheel.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Dakota answers that the electric wheel is their main priority and the small bike is just a fun side project.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Chris jokes that the small bike is as fast as the Dallas Mavericks' non-existent playoff highlight reel.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Dakota fires back at Chris, joking that Chris does not even own a basketball team to have any highlights.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin reacts with loud amusement to Dakota's quick comeback against Chris's sports joke.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Chris laughs and asks if Dakota's only comeback is the fact that Chris does not own a basketball team.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin remarks that Dakota's joke was a very good zinger against Chris.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Chris states he wants to invest in long-term electric native bikes rather than retrofitted ones, and exits the deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michael asserts his belief that retrofitting current items to make them electric vehicles represents the true future.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark cites the intensely competitive environment of selling bikes against big box retailers as his primary reason to exit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michael thanks Mark and attempts to add more information about their future business model and distribution plans.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michael explains their plan to grow from direct-to-consumer sales to providing fleets for delivery services and police departments.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark argues that every motorized vehicle company is also targeting those same fleet and delivery service markets.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michael counters that police and delivery services do not need to buy entirely new bikes, giving them an advantage.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori acknowledges that Michael has made a valid point regarding the fleet market strategy.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Michael emphasizes that police departments and bike share programs already have their current fleets of traditional bicycles.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Mark argues that the nine hundred and fifty dollar price tag will still be a significant hurdle for those fleets.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Lori states the product lacks an affordable price, which violates one of her rules for a great product, and exits.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin says he would buy the small bike but thinks the company needs to lower costs, so he exits.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Barbara finds the price too high and cannot picture herself swapping the wheel, leading her to exit the deal.

decisions.note: Wants to invest in long-term electric native bikes, not retrofitted ones.
Intensely competitive environment selling bikes against big box retailers.
Needs more iterations to lower cost; wants the small bike but not the company.
Price is too high and cannot picture herself swapping the wheel.
